summary: Bloom Energy makes solid-oxide fuel cells for on-site power, heavily dependent on natural gas supply and rare-earth materials in its electrolytic layers. Its key risk is concentrated upstream nickel/cobalt sourcing and single-source balance-of-plant components; demand is tied to data-center and industrial uptime, making it vulnerable to an AI capex slowdown.

inputs.whyNeeded: Core solid-oxide stack requires rare-earth and specialty metals for performance and durability
inputs.concentration: High: ~70% of global nickel refinement in Indonesia/China; rare-earth processing ~90% in China
inputs.fragility: High: geopolitical/trade-war risk; price volatility from EV battery demand competes for nickel

inputs.whyNeeded: Key electrolyte layer in fuel cell; sourced from few specialty ceramic suppliers
inputs.concentration: Moderate: limited specialist vendors (e.g., CeramTec, Tosoh) but substitutes via alternative formulations possible
inputs.fragility: Moderate: single-sourcing risk per product variant, but tech flexibility allows reformulation over 6-12 months

inputs.node: Natural gas (fuel input for most installations)
inputs.whyNeeded: Primary fuel for Bloom Energy Servers; price and availability drive operating cost
inputs.concentration: Diverse: US shale gas (spot/renewable nat gas) but pipeline/infrastructure access is project-specific
inputs.fragility: Low-Moderate: supply diversified, but region-specific price spikes (winter storms) can hurt margins

chokepoints.node: Single-source balance-of-plant (BoP) components (power inverters, heat exchangers)
chokepoints.why: Proprietary designs limit qualified vendors; any disruption from key component maker (e.g., Danfoss) halts production
Over 90% of rare-earth processing in China; export controls or price spikes directly raise stack cost

chokepoints.node: Tariffs on Chinese nickel and cobalt imports
chokepoints.why: US trade policy could double input costs; no quick domestic substitute for high-purity nickel

customers.why: Largest demand driver for on-site fuel cells; 24/7 reliability for AI/cloud workloads; contracts are long-term
Manufacturing facilities, hospitals, campuses seeking backup or primary power; lower growth but stable
Regulatory support for fuel cells; but geopolitical/subsidy risk and currency exposure

geographic: Inputs concentrated in China and Indonesia; manufacturing in US (California, Delaware); customer installations primarily in US data centers, some in South Korea and Europe.
substitutes: Battery storage + grid (lower up-front cost, but less reliable for 24/7 uptime); natural gas turbines (lower efficiency, higher emissions); nuclear microreactors (higher cost, longer timeline)

bearCase: Tariffs or export controls on nickel/cobalt/rare-earths push stack cost up 20-30%, eroding margin and competitiveness.
A single-source BoP supplier has a 6-month disruption (e.g., factory fire), halting delivery of all systems and triggering order cancellations.
AI/cloud capex slows in 2026/27 due to overbuild or regulation; data-center contract pipeline dries up, forcing revenue miss.
Natural gas price spikes (e.g., winter storm Uri repeat) make fuel cell operating cost uncompetitive vs grid for critical loads.
South Korean subsidy cuts reduce international volume by 40%+.

loadBearing.assumption: Rare-earth/nickel supply remains available at current prices +-10%.
loadBearing.breaksIf: China imposes rare-earth export quotas or US tariffs on Chinese processed nickel, cratering gross margin.

loadBearing.assumption: No major disruption at single-source BoP supplier.
loadBearing.breaksIf: A 6-month+ interruption at that supplier (e.g., natural disaster or labor strike) stops all shipments.

loadBearing.assumption: US data-center construction and AI-driven power demand continue growing >15% y/y.
loadBearing.breaksIf: Hyperscalers pause new data-center buildouts due to AI bubble concerns or regulatory overhang.

loadBearing.assumption: South Korean RD&D subsidy program continues at current levels.
loadBearing.breaksIf: Government budget cuts or shift to hydrogen reduce 2026-27 orders.

prediction.statement: Q2 2026 earnings (late August 2026) will show >25% y/y revenue growth but gross margin compression to 23-25% from 27% due to nickel/rare-earth cost headwinds, causing stock to fail to recover and trade down to $200-210.
prediction.resolutionCriterion: Actual Q2 revenue growth and gross margin reported in next quarterly result; if revenue growth <20% or gross margin <23%, prediction confirmed.

diminishingReturns: Stopped at rare-earth and BoP component level; deeper hops (e.g., yttrium mine ownership or inverter transistor supply) do not change investment picture because price/availability shocks dominate and have no quick substitutes regardless of sub-sub-supplier.
